topics.name: Embeddings & Vector Stores
topics.description: Representing text as vectors for similarity search.
notes: - 把文本转换成向量，语义相近的文本向量距离更近。
- 同一套检索中，文档和查询必须使用同一个 embedding 模型。
- 保存文档向量及原文、元数据，支持查询最相似的 k 个结果。
- 相似度常用余弦相似度或点积。

topics.name: Retrieval Pipeline
topics.description: Indexing and retrieval steps of a RAG system.
notes: - 加载文档，切分成块（chunk），向量化，写入向量库。
- 块太大噪声多，块太小会丢失上下文，需要结合重叠长度调整。
- 把用户问题向量化，检索最相关的块，拼入提示词交给模型回答。
- RAG 通过提供外部上下文来回答，不需要修改模型权重。
- 可要求模型基于检索内容作答并引用来源，以减少幻觉。

questions.title: Which rule must hold when using embeddings for retrieval?

options.text: Documents and queries must be embedded with the same embedding model
Queries must be longer than documents
Each document needs its own embedding model
Embeddings must be regenerated for every query

questions.explanation: Vectors from different models live in different spaces and cannot be compared meaningfully.

questions.title: The store holds 10 documents. What is printed?
questions.codeSnippet:
results = vector_store.similarity_search(
    "How do I reset my password?", k=3
)
print(len(results))

options.text: 0, because the query must be embedded manually first

questions.explanation: k is the number of nearest documents to return. The store embeds the query itself.

questions.title: A cosine similarity close to 1 between two embeddings means:

options.text: The vectors point in nearly the same direction, so the texts are semantically similar
The texts contain exactly the same characters
The texts are unrelated
One text is a translation error

questions.explanation: Cosine similarity compares direction. Values near 1 indicate similar meaning, not identical wording.

questions.title: Fill in the parameter that keeps context across neighboring chunks.
questions.codeSnippet:
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter

splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
    chunk_size=1000, ______=200
)
chunks = splitter.split_documents(docs)

options.text: chunk_overlap
chunk_stride
chunk_margin
overlap_size

questions.explanation: chunk_overlap sets how many characters neighboring chunks share.

questions.title: Why do text splitters usually use a chunk overlap?

options.text: So that information at a chunk boundary is not lost
To reduce the number of chunks
To make embeddings cheaper
To remove duplicate documents

questions.explanation: A sentence cut in half at a boundary would otherwise be unreadable in both chunks. Overlap preserves context at the cost of some duplication.

questions.title: The answers ignore the knowledge base. What is the bug?

options.text: The retrieved documents are never added to the prompt
retriever.invoke needs a list of questions
The model must be fine-tuned on docs
print() hides the context

questions.explanation: Retrieval only helps if the retrieved text is placed in the prompt sent to the model.

questions.title: What property makes embeddings useful for retrieval?

options.text: Texts with similar meaning are mapped to vectors that are close together
They compress text losslessly so it can be restored exactly
They remove the need for a vector store
They translate text into SQL

questions.explanation: Similarity search compares the query vector with stored document vectors and returns the nearest ones.

questions.title: Which steps are typically part of the indexing phase of a RAG system?

options.text: Load documents
Split documents into chunks
Embed the chunks and store them in a vector store
Fine-tune the base model weights on every document

questions.explanation: Indexing loads, splits, embeds and stores content. Retrieval later finds relevant chunks and passes them to the model as context. RAG does not require changing model weights.
